dimensions.label: Problem Clarity
dimensions.evidence: Season 1's badges are ephemeral (recomputed client-side against a rolling window, can silently un-earn) and officers have no way to manually recognize things that can't be rule-verified (e.g. self-reported recipes).

dimensions.label: Goal Definition
dimensions.evidence: Every rule-satisfied tier crossing and every manual grant produces exactly one permanent achievement_award row, scoped correctly to season or all-time; unseen awards drive a FAB-triggered reveal that marks seenAt on dismiss.

dimensions.label: Success Criteria
dimensions.evidence: 9 rule shapes each have a synthetic-data vitest case, plus idempotency, append-per-crossing, season/all-time window correctness, family-level attribution, manual-grant scope-gating, and old-system removal — see successCriteria.

dimensions.label: Scope Boundaries
dimensions.evidence: MVP/full/out-of-scope explicitly enumerated: rip-and-replace Season 1 (archived to docs first), 9 achievements (one per shape) plus one all-time example, recipes are manual-grant-only, QStash-triggered evaluation, full reveal wiring.

dimensions.label: Consistency
dimensions.evidence: Permanence (never revoked) and season-scoping (window clips to [season.start, now]) operate at different layers — the window decides what CAN evaluate true; once true, it freezes forever. No unresolved contradictions surfaced.

problem: Temple Era guild raiders have no permanent record of what they've accomplished in a season. Season 1's badge system is evaluated entirely client-side, on every render, against a rolling 6-week attendance window — a badge a raider held last month can silently vanish this month as the window rolls forward, even though they genuinely earned it. There is no fanfare, no persistent trophy case, and no way for an officer to manually recognize something that can't be reduced to a rule (Season 1's recipe data is self-reported and can be temporarily faked, so it can never be trusted for automated verification).

Season 2 needs achievements that are permanent once earned, evaluated by rule against actual data scoped correctly to a season's own lockout weeks (never bleeding in pre-season history) or, for a smaller set of exceptionally hard achievements, across all history — with room for officers to manually grant recognition outside the rule engine entirely.
goals: Every tier crossing (bronze through platinum) that a rule is satisfied for during its correct window — season-clipped or all-time — is captured exactly once as a permanent achievement_award row, keyed to the family that earned it, with no duplicates and no missed crossings.

A family that goes bronze then later silver on the same achievement ends up with two permanent, individually-replayable award rows, while still being trivially queryable for 'current highest tier' per achievement per season.

A raider with unseen awards sees a badged FAB on the dashboard; clicking it plays the already-validated reveal ceremony (hero + strip for multiple awards) against real data, every image preloaded before the sequence starts.
Dismissing the reveal marks seenAt for every shown award; a new Trophy Case surface lets a raider replay any past reveal on demand, independent of seen state.
Season 1's ephemeral badge system is fully retired — code removed, its old achievement/rule definitions preserved only as documentation — replaced entirely by the new permanent model.
The rule engine supports all 9 identified rule shapes, plus the season-bound/all-time scope dimension, as pure configuration — a new achievement requires no new engineering, only new data.

Visible achievements show, on both the character page and the Trophy Case, the highest tier a family has earned plus a progress bar toward the next tier; hidden achievements occupy no display space at all until the family earns their first tier of one, after which earned hidden achievements surface in a dedicated 'Hidden Achievements Earned' section — never revealing an unearned hidden achievement's existence.

successCriteria.criterion: Achievement schema (season, achievement, achievement_tier, achievement_award) typechecks and Drizzle relations compile.
Raid Attendance (threshold-over-window) awards the correct tier at each boundary against synthetic lockout-week data (e.g. 59%/4wk = none, 60%/4wk = bronze, 100%/10wk = platinum).

Consistency (same-character signup↔attend match) requires BOTH an early-checkpoint confirmed signup AND matching actual attendance by that same character; a synthetic case with only one half does not award. An ambiguous or unmatched signup-to-character match (match-signups.ts's MatchStatus) is excluded, not counted.

Flexibility (cross-character family signup↔attend match) awards when the signed-up and attending characters differ but share a family, and does not award when the attending character isn't linked to the signed-up one. An ambiguous or unmatched signup match is excluded, not counted.
Bench Credit (discrete event count) increments only on bench-classified signup buckets against synthetic multi-raid signup history.
Zone Attendance (per-zone threshold) evaluates each 40-man raid zone independently — attendance in one zone doesn't count toward another zone's tier.
Raid Marathon (per-week raid density) counts distinct raids attended within a single lockout week, not raw attendance count across weeks.
Zone Breadth (per-window zone breadth) counts distinct zones raided within a window; attending the same zone twice does not double-count.
Class Breadth (per-window class breadth) counts distinct classes the family raided as within a season window.
Family Double-Up (per-raid family co-occurrence) awards when two characters from the same family both appear in one raid's attendee set.
An all-time-scoped achievement (reusing the Class Breadth rule, unbounded window) counts qualifying data from a season two seasons prior — all-time scope is NOT clipped to the current season.
A season-bound achievement's window clips to [season.startDate, now] — synthetic qualifying data from before the season start does not count toward it.
Evaluation is idempotent — running the same evaluation twice against unchanged data produces zero duplicate achievement_award rows.
Crossing bronze then later silver on the same achievement within one season produces two permanent rows, not one overwritten row, and 'current highest tier' is trivially queryable from them.

A new achievement definition that reuses an existing rule shape (e.g. a second all-time Class Breadth variant) can be added in achievement-definitions.ts alone, with zero diff to achievement-rules.ts, and evaluates correctly — proving goal 6's 'no new engineering, only new data' claim.

Each rule shape's evaluator exposes a raw progress value (current metric, next tier's threshold) alongside tier-crossing pass/fail, computed from the same window/scope logic — not a second parallel implementation.

A visible achievement always renders on the character page and the Trophy Case with its highest earned tier (or 'not yet earned') and a progress bar toward the next tier; a hidden achievement renders nowhere until the family earns its first tier of it, after which it appears only inside a Hidden Achievements Earned section on both surfaces.

check.judgment: reviewer seeds one visible achievement mid-progress and one hidden achievement (unearned, then earned) and checks both surfaces reflect the correct display state

successCriteria.criterion: Creating a custom award definition (name, icon, tier, season|all-time scope, no rule attached) and granting it are two separate achievement:manage-scoped mutations — an unscoped session is rejected from both, and the same definition can be granted to multiple different families over time, each grant producing its own achievement_award row.
A dedicated mark-seen mutation sets seenAt on every achievement_award row passed to it, scoped to the calling user's own family, and is idempotent if called twice.
The QStash evaluation route rejects an unsigned request and, given a valid signed request, evaluates only the triggering raid's attendees against a synthetic roster.
Season 1's badge-definitions.ts, badge-evaluator.ts, and character-badges.tsx are deleted, and their content is preserved in a written archive doc.

decisions.decision: Attribution is family-level (primaryCharacterId) — matches how attendance already aggregates across a character's alts

decisions.decision: Permanence is append-per-crossing — a new row for every tier crossed, never overwritten

decisions.decision: A rule engine covering 9 generalized shapes is core scope, not hardcoded per-achievement logic
decisions.rejected: Hardcoded evaluation with no rule engine (the orphaned contract's out-of-scope call)
decisions.reason: this session's interview drove toward an explicit, reusable rule-shape taxonomy across attendance, signups, and family structure — superseding the earlier, less-informed exclusion

decisions.decision: Diamond tier is NOT reserved exclusively for all-time achievements; all-time achievements can use the full bronze→platinum ladder like season-bound ones
decisions.rejected: Diamond = all-time-only capstone tier, reviving the orphaned contract's + mockup's existing diamond tier design

decisions.decision: Phase 3 ports only the bronze→platinum reveal choreography; the mockup's diamond buildup/supernova path stays unported reference until a concrete diamond achievement exists
decisions.rejected: Port the full ladder including diamond now, since the mockup already built it

decisions.decision: Achievement evaluation fires from two hook points — after mutateInsertRaidLogWithAttendees succeeds, AND again after runPostRaidCreationSignupLinking resolves in POST /api/v1/raids
decisions.rejected: A single hook on mutateInsertRaidLogWithAttendees only
decisions.reason: hidden-dependency critic finding — Consistency/Flexibility depend on raidSignupSnapshotLinks, which is created later by a separate, unrelated request; evaluation is already idempotent (criterion 13) so firing twice is safe and simpler than guaranteeing one exact ordering

decisions.decision: Ambiguous or unmatched Raid Helper signup matches (match-signups.ts's MatchStatus) are excluded from Consistency/Flexibility evaluation, not counted
decisions.reason: hidden-dependency critic flagged this as previously unspecified; excluding is the conservative default that avoids awarding on an uncertain identity match

decisions.decision: Zone Attendance ships in MVP with one achievement per 40-man raid zone the guild clears this season (Onyxia and 20-man raids excluded), not a single current-zone achievement with the rest deferred
decisions.rejected: MVP ships one Zone Attendance achievement for the current raid tier's zone only; remaining zones deferred to Stretch

decisions.decision: Achievements can be hidden or visible; visible ones show highest-tier-earned plus a progress bar toward the next tier on the character page and Trophy Case; hidden ones occupy no display space until first earned, then move into a dedicated Hidden Achievements Earned section on both surfaces
decisions.rejected: All achievements always visible with a locked/grayed state, no hidden concept and no progress display
decisions.reason: user specified this directly — mirrors Season 1's hidden-badge concept but adds progress-bar display for visible achievements and a distinct post-first-earn reveal section for hidden ones

execution.strategy: Hybrid: a sequential foundation (schema) unlocks two parallel phases (rule engine, reveal UI), which converge before a final cleanup phase removes the old system.

phases.title: Season + Achievement Schema + Manual Grant
phases.notes: season, achievement, achievement_tier, achievement_award (family-level, append-per-crossing, season|all-time scope) Drizzle schema + migration; achievement:manage scope added to scopes.ts + role-editor.tsx description map; two-step manual admin flow as its own tRPC procedures — createAchievement (definition only, no rule) and grantAchievement (definition + family -> new award row, repeatable) — plus minimal admin UI for both. Season 2's real start/end date is provided later by the user (~Sept-Dec) and seeded as a follow-up data change once known — tests use a synthetic season, this phase does not block on the real date.

phases.title: Rule Engine + 9 Achievement Definitions
phases.notes: Rule evaluator supporting all 9 shapes plus season-bound vs. all-time window resolution; concrete achievement definitions (illustrative thresholds, tunable later) — one per non-zone shape plus the all-time example, and Zone Attendance defined once per 40-man raid zone the guild clears this season (Onyxia and 20-man raids excluded); idempotency; append-per-crossing with an easy 'current highest tier' query/view. No precedent in this codebase for server-side rule evaluation at this complexity — highest-risk phase. Consistency/Flexibility resolve signups via match-signups.ts's heuristic matcher (raidSignupSnapshotLinks), whose MatchStatus can be ambiguous or unmatched, not just matched — only matched signups count toward those two shapes. Each rule-shape test title should encode its key boundary values (e.g. 'attendance: 59%@4wk=none, 60%@4wk=bronze, 100%@10wk=platinum') so coverage is verifiable by title alone, not just tag presence. Each shape's evaluator also returns a raw progress value (current metric vs. next tier's threshold) for display, computed via the same window/scope logic as tier-crossing — not a second implementation.

phases.title: Reveal Overlay + FAB + Trophy Case
phases.notes: Can develop against manually-granted awards from Phase 1 alone, in parallel with Phase 2. Ports the validated docs/followups/mockups/reveal-overlay.html choreography into a real React component, bronze through platinum only — the mockup's diamond buildup/supernova path is not ported (see decisions and scope.future); dashboard FAB; preload-before-play; seenAt-on-dismiss (calls Phase 1's mark-seen mutation); Trophy Case page with replay button, linked from app-header.tsx so it's reachable from navigation, not just by URL. Also adds the shared achievement-display component (highest tier earned + progress bar toward next tier for visible achievements; hidden achievements invisible until first earned, then shown in a Hidden Achievements Earned section) used on both the Trophy Case and the character page, replacing character-badges.tsx's old slot in character-detail.tsx.

phases.title: QStash Evaluation Trigger
phases.notes: New api/qstash/achievement-evaluate route following the existing discovery/capture pattern. Fires from TWO hook points, both idempotent (criterion 13 covers safety): (1) after mutateInsertRaidLogWithAttendees succeeds, covering the 7 shapes that don't depend on signup data; (2) after runPostRaidCreationSignupLinking resolves in POST /api/v1/raids, re-evaluating so Consistency/Flexibility see the now-created raidSignupSnapshotLinks — raid-log import and signup-link creation are separate, sequential requests, so a single hook would miss those two shapes' dependency (hidden-dependency critic finding).

phases.title: Retire Season 1 Badges
phases.notes: Archive Season 1's badge definitions/rules to docs/followups/season-1-badges-archive.md, then delete badge-definitions.ts, badge-evaluator.ts, character-badges.tsx and its usage. Sequenced last so the new system is proven live before the old one is removed.
